original.statement: Crossplane v2.0.0 removes the --registry CLI flag, requiring users to always specify fully qualified URLs when installing packages instead of relying on a default registry value.

decision.reason: [ev-792eae516f7e] is one Backward compatibility section that lists five separate breaking changes: removal of native patch and transform composition, removal of ControllerConfig, removal of external secret stores, removal of composite resource connection details, and removal of the default registry. The question asks about the patch and transform removal, but the proposed exposure (cli-flag --registry set) covers only the default-registry change, so it does not match the change being asked about. The evidence does not name the fields that would show a patch-and-transform Composition is in use, so no correct exposure condition for that change follows from it. Because the source bundles unrelated changes, each one needs its own assertion.
